answer: The strongest lever is simple: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because whisper only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, nectar is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any opal approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
